C0.quote: subgame perfect implementability of compromise rules, as a function of the compromise threshold
C0.note: Strategic (implementation via equilibria of mechanisms) analysis of voting rules such as scoring, Condorcet, compromise rules.

C1.quote: Condition β, for subgame perfect implementability
C1.note: Main results show which voting rules satisfy Conditions alpha/beta (necessary/sufficient for SPE implementability). Coded AX primary because results are property checks; EQ because the property is equilibrium implementability.

C2.2.quote: complete, transitive and antisymmetric binary relations on X
C2.2.note: Linear orders; rules (e.g. majority relation, compromise rules) are computed from the rankings.

C2.3.quote: Each agent i ∈ N is endowed with a preference relation

C2.4.quote: A social choice rule (SCR) is a correspondence f : P n → A
C2.4.note: Rule is defined directly on preference profiles. Footnote 10 says 'each voter announces a ranking' for plurality with runoff but no separate notation for messages or reports; no statement of equality or difference.

C3.1.quote: implemented via subgame perfect equilibria of extensive form mechanisms
C3.1.note: Every main result concerns SPE implementability, which presupposes strategic agents in a mechanism; formal results are checks of Condition alpha/beta, so strategic behaviour is background rather than modelled in the text.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare, satisfaction or cost notions used.

C5.1.note: Only implementability and consistency with Condorcet; Pareto optimality appears only in footnote 3 as a literature result on Maskin monotonicity, not a claim of the paper.

VOT.quote_behav: implemented via subgame perfect equilibria of extensive form mechanisms
VOT.note: Agents are the players of the mechanism, playing SPE. Information structure is not stated; it is only inherited by reference to Abreu and Sen [1990].

DES.note: Mechanism existence is a property of the rule; designer's choice or objective is not modelled as an agent.

C8.2.quote: implementable via subgame perfect equilibria of extensive form mechanisms

C9.1.note: Conclusion makes claims about implementability and the Borda-Condorcet tension, not about real institutions, voters' well-being or which rule to use.
